s01.heading: 01 / PROJECT OVERVIEW
s01.p1:
Unseen Witness is a 2D pixel-art narrative adventure game about understanding, companionship, and farewell.

Players take on the role of Ashe, spending time with her close friend Power in a familiar campus environment. As the story unfolds, Ashe gradually enters Power's inner world, attempting to understand feelings that cannot always be expressed through exploration, interaction, and everyday acts of companionship.
s01.meta4: Scope: 4 Chapters, including a Main Menu and Chapter Replay System
s01.meta5: My Responsibilities: Game Design, Narrative Design, Dialogue and Quest Writing, Level Design, 2D Art Direction, UI Design, and Unity Implementation
s01.keywords: Keywords: Companionship / Subjective Perception / Environmental Storytelling / Emotional Interaction

s02.heading: 02 / DESIGN MOTIVATION
s02.p1: Unseen Witness is rooted in my real-life experience with a close friend. Ashe is based on me, while Power is inspired by my friend. Our relationship has involved everyday conflicts, misunderstandings, and emotions that were often difficult to express.
s02.p2: I have never witnessed the hallucinations Power described—shadow figures, pale figures, and spectral faces. I could only learn about her perceptual experiences through her words, trying to understand a world beyond my own perception. This made me realize that even people who are close to each other may experience reality differently. For people living with mental illness, the distress they experience can be deeply real and overwhelming, yet remain invisible to those around them. We can listen, care, and offer companionship, but that does not necessarily mean we truly understand what they are going through.
s02.p3: Today, I am preparing to pursue graduate studies overseas, while she remains in China, receiving regular treatment and beginning her professional life. We are still close friends and stay in touch every day. Rather than recreating our experiences literally, I wanted to reinterpret the emotions, misunderstandings, and relationships within them through game design, while creating an opportunity for more people to approach experiences that are often difficult to understand.
s02.p4: When misunderstandings arise between close friends, can listening, communication, and shared experiences help them understand each other and bridge the distance between them?
s02.p5: This question became the foundation of the game's design. Players explore overlooked clues, enter Power's world of perception, accompany her through everyday life, and reflect on the impact of their own actions. I wanted players to discover not only what a character is going through, but also the feelings left unspoken and the things they have yet to understand through their own observations, actions, and choices.
s02.p6: For me, Unseen Witness is more than a story about friendship; it is also an exploration of interactive storytelling. Through gameplay, I hope to bring players closer to the inner experiences of people living with mental illness, while encouraging them to reconsider how they understand and support those whose worlds may differ from their own.

c1.title: Chapter 01 — Waiting and Misunderstanding
c1.lead: Making the Passage of Time Tangible
c1.p1: The story begins with an everyday misunderstanding. Power tells Ashe that she is going to the restroom but does not return for a long time. As the wait continues, Ashe gradually loses patience and eventually leaves on her own, unaware that Power has been feeling physically unwell.
c1.p2:
Through interactive classroom objects, classmates gradually leaving, changing lighting, and the darkening sky, players experience the passage of time firsthand. When a similar situation occurs again, Power tells Ashe that she is unwell, and Ashe begins to actively look for and care about her.

By making time and the surrounding environment change, this chapter guides players from initial frustration toward a reconsideration of Power's situation.

c2.title: Chapter 02 — Entering Power's World of Perception
c2.lead: Turning Invisible Feelings into an Explorable Space
c2.p1: Ashe enters a distorted labyrinth built around a familiar restroom environment. Everyday objects lose their original order, while the structure and proportions of the space become increasingly illogical. Players must explore the labyrinth, avoid monsters, and search for clues to gradually approach Power's inner world.
c2.p2: The visual designs are based on Power's personal descriptions of her experiences. They are not intended as literal reproductions of real symptoms, but rather as artistic interpretations that translate her descriptions of fear, feeling watched, and conflicting emotions into explorable environments and characters.

black.name: Shadow Figures
black.tag: Shadow figures · persistent threat and fear
black.title: Shadow Figures — Persistent Fear
black.p1:
Power described frequently seeing shadow figures at night, appearing on the floor, beside her bed, on the ceiling, or outside her window. These were among the most memorable and recurring images in her descriptions.

I designed them as the labyrinth's primary monsters. Their repeated appearances and pursuit create a persistent sense of unease and tension throughout the exploration.

white.name: Pale Figures
white.title: Pale Figures — The Conflict Between Defense and the Desire to Be Understood
white.p1: Unlike the shadow figures, the pale figures Power described usually remained still and did not directly provoke fear. I designed them as ambiguous guides: they sometimes block Ashe's path, yet also leave clues that encourage her to move forward.
white.p2: Their contradictory behavior represents Power's tendency to withdraw from and defend herself against the outside world, while still holding a desire to be understood by someone close to her.

ghost.name: Spectral Faces
ghost.tag: Spectral faces · fear of being watched and discussed
ghost.title: Spectral Faces — The Oppression of Being Watched and Talked About
ghost.p1:
Power also described seeing spectral faces appear unexpectedly and feeling that people around her were talking about her. I translated these descriptions into sudden, frightening encounters that interrupt the player's exploration.

Through brief visual shocks, these appearances convey the oppressive feeling of being watched and discussed by others.

env.title: Distorted Environment — The Loss of Familiarity and Order
env.p1: Beyond the monsters, the labyrinth itself reflects Power's subjective perception. Everyday objects appear in unreasonable places, spatial structures become distorted, and familiar surroundings gradually lose their sense of order. The environmental design also draws inspiration from the film The Backrooms, particularly its treatment of ordinary spaces becoming unfamiliar and unsettling.
env.p2: The enormous distorted figure of Ashe is also part of this environmental distortion. Power once described how, even when Ashe did not intend to criticize her, she sometimes experienced Ashe's words as an attack. I translated this into an imposing, oversized figure, prompting Ashe to reflect on her impatient temperament and how her seemingly casual words might affect Power.

end.p1: At the end of the labyrinth, the pale figures begin questioning Ashe. Their questions shift the player's attention from what Power has experienced to how Ashe has treated her, and whether her own behavior may have deepened their misunderstandings.
end.p2: Understanding another person also requires examining ourselves.

c3.title: Chapter 03 — Companionship in Everyday Life
c3.p1: After leaving the labyrinth, Ashe begins accompanying Power through everyday campus life. Players help them eat together, complete daily tasks, remember medication, and respond when Power feels unwell.
c3.p2: This chapter unfolds over three consecutive days on campus. As time passes, Power's condition gradually worsens, making everyday tasks increasingly difficult. Ashe must respond to more and more needs, yet begins to realize that she cannot control how things unfold.
c3.p3: Ashe cannot cure Power, but she can choose to stay by her side.

c4.title: Chapter 04 — Gifts & Farewell
c4.lead: Memories that cannot be taken along
c4.p1: Due to the uncertainty surrounding her treatment and future, Power ultimately cannot accompany Ashe abroad. Before they part ways, she invites Ashe to choose a few gifts from her room to take along.
c4.p3: The selected gifts remain on the main menu after the story ends. They become tangible traces of the time the two spent together, allowing the player's choices to carry on beyond the game itself.
c4.p2: The bus stop scene appears at both the beginning and the end of the game, creating a visual parallel. At the beginning, Ashe and Power stand side by side at the bus stop. By the end, Ashe is left standing alone. The recurring setting highlights the changes in their circumstances and relationship, while Power's absence becomes a quiet yet powerful expression of loss.

m1.title: Chapter 02 — Exploration, Clue Collection & Hallucination Encounters
m1.lead: Understand Power's world through exploration and encounters with her hallucinations.
m1.p1: Players navigate a surreal bathroom labyrinth, observing their surroundings, searching for key objects, and solving puzzles. Environmental anomalies, monster behaviors, and clues left by the Pale Figures gradually reveal more about Power's experiences and emotions.
m1.p2: In this chapter, Ashe has 100 points of Will. Coming into contact with different hallucinations reduces her Will by different amounts:
m1.b1: Shadow Figures: Contact reduces Will by 10 points.
m1.b2: Spectral Faces: Contact reduces Will by 20 points.
m1.p3: Players can right-click to release Will, a burst of determination that breaks through the hallucinations in front of Ashe. Three consecutive uses of Will can eliminate Shadow Figures, while Spectral Faces cannot be attacked and must be avoided.
m1.p4: These mechanics turn the fear and pressure Power experiences into tangible gameplay challenges, requiring players to assess risks and adapt their strategies while exploring.
m1.p5: Rather than passively receiving background information, players piece together Power's subjective world through observation, experimentation, deduction, and encounters with the hallucinations.

design.heading: Exploring and Refining the Maze Design
design.initialP: Initially, I planned to create a single, complete top-down maze map, where players would navigate in four directions to find the correct exit within a fixed layout. However, this approach felt too similar to a conventional maze game. The exploration quickly became repetitive, and it was difficult to convey the disorienting, oppressive, and eerie atmosphere I envisioned.
design.finalLabel: 02 — Final Direction: Endless Corridors and Sequential Exploration
design.finalP: I eventually shifted to a maze built around interconnected corridors and rooms. Players must continually open doors and enter unfamiliar spaces, searching for a way forward through environments that appear familiar yet subtly distorted. By obscuring clear spatial boundaries and limiting players' ability to anticipate what lies beyond each door, this approach creates a stronger sense of disorientation, uncertainty, and psychological tension.

m2.title: Chapter 03 — Companion System & Stamina Management
m2.p1: Power's stamina reflects her ability to move and her current condition in the game. During campus activities, players must keep track of her position and stamina, adjusting their movements according to the distance between the two characters.
m2.b1: Moving Together: Power continuously loses stamina while following Ashe.
m2.b2: Waiting: When Power stays still and Ashe is nearby, her stamina no longer decreases.
m2.b3: Distance: The farther Ashe moves away from Power, the faster her stamina drains.
m2.b4: State Feedback: When Power's stamina reaches zero, she experiences hallucinations and the current task fails. Players must restart the task.
m2.b5: Condition Progression: Power's stamina drains progressively faster from Chapter 1 to Chapter 3, reflecting the worsening of her condition.
m2.p2: This system serves both gameplay and narrative purposes. On a gameplay level, players must manage the distance between the two characters and adjust their pace. On a narrative level, they must actively look after Power rather than completing everything on their own.
m2.p3: Staying close and waiting for Power allow her to continue participating in everyday life, but they cannot prevent her condition from worsening. Companionship is not a cure, but an ongoing choice to stay by someone's side.

m3.title: Chapter 04 — Free Gift Selection & State Persistence
m3.lead: Turning player choices into a visible gameplay experience.
m3.p1: Players can freely choose which gifts to take from Power's room, with no minimum requirement and a maximum of 19 items. The selection includes a variety of objects, ranging from ordinary items such as plush toys to unexpected and humorous choices like dog food, a moldy orange, or even a complete set of knight's armor.
m3.p3: By combining diverse item selections, character interactions, and personalized visual outcomes, this mechanic adds a layer of playful discovery while offering a lighthearted contrast to the game's otherwise somber tone.

s05.heading: 05 / DESIGN DEEP DIVE: CHAPTER 3'S DAILY SCHEDULE AND COMPANION SYSTEM
s05.p1:
Organizing Three Days of Everyday Life into a Functional System

Chapter 3 reuses the same campus map throughout three days. Changes in dates, time stages, task states, and character behaviors gradually transform the player's everyday experience.

d1.design: Establish the basic companion system and task flow, including having lunch together, returning to the classroom, and medication reminders.
d1.exp: Become familiar with the basic rules of the companion system.

d2.design: Introduce additional campus activities, such as completing classroom duties and purchasing essential items, expanding the variety of daily tasks.
d2.exp: Develop proficiency in using the companion system and gain a deeper understanding of its mechanics through a wider range of everyday situations.

d3.design: Power's condition continues to deteriorate, eventually leaving her unable to follow Ashe or participate in daily tasks. She ultimately collapses from exhaustion.
d3.exp: Experience a sense of helplessness and frustration as Power's condition worsens despite the player's efforts to accompany her.

s05.trade: Rather than building three separate environments for the three days, I chose to reuse the campus map and control tasks, character behaviors, and event triggers through schedule and state changes. This preserves spatial continuity while allowing development efforts to focus on character interactions and system integration.

s06.heading: 06 / VISUAL AND UI DESIGN
s06.p1:
Using Visual Changes to Distinguish Reality from Subjective Perception

The game uses a top-down 2D pixel-art style. Campus environments emphasize clear spatial layouts and a familiar everyday atmosphere, while the labyrinth uses spatial distortions, lighting changes, and unusual objects to create an unstable perceptual experience.
s06.p2: The UI maintains a consistent visual language while distinguishing dialogue, interaction prompts, and task information. The main menu combines a bus stop setting with the display of selected gifts, allowing the player's final choices to remain part of the game interface.

s07.heading: 07 / TECHNICAL IMPLEMENTATION
s07.p1:
From Narrative Design to Functional Game Systems

The project was independently developed using Unity and C#. A complete game framework was built around level progression, task states, and character interactions.
s07.b1: Dialogue and Quest System: Organizes character dialogue and quest content through data-driven dialogue resources.
s07.b2: Schedule and Event System: Manages time progression, task states, and event triggers in Chapter 3.
s07.b3: Area Management: Switches camera views and activity boundaries between different areas within the same scene.
s07.b4: Companion Behavior System: Implements Power's follow, wait, event-pause, and behavior-resume states.
s07.b5: Level Flow and Save System: Manages the four chapters, chapter replay, and persistent gift selections.

s08.heading: 08 / REFLECTION
s08.p1: Understanding Does Not Mean Being Able to Change Everything.
s08.p2:
During development, I gradually realized that translating an emotional theme into an effective gameplay experience is much more challenging than simply writing a moving story.

Chapter 2 invites players into Power's subjective world of perception, while Chapter 3 turns understanding into everyday actions. Ultimately, I hope players remember not that Ashe saved Power, but that even when she could not change everything, she still chose to understand and accompany her friend through part of that journey.
s08.p3: In future iterations, I would like to further refine the puzzle pacing in Chapter 2, expand NPC side quests and task feedback in Chapter 3, and introduce accessibility options such as adjustable subtitle sizes and text speed.

s09.heading: 09 / BEYOND THE GAME
s09.p1: Unseen Witness is inspired by the real-life experiences I shared with my close friend, Power. The characters Ashe and Power are not entirely fictional creations, but are reimagined through the memories and moments we shared.
s09.p2: This page brings together glimpses of the real lives behind the game, including moments with Power and her dog, Lucky. These memories are where the story began, and what Unseen Witness hopes to preserve.
